subject: Follow-up: Greenline throughput mix & burst profile
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Sam White <sam.white@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Greenline throughput mix & burst profile

Hi Sam — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can turn this into a sizing recommendation and a short tech workshop with infra: 

1) Workload profile (what I captured from the call)
- Steady-state: ~10–15 QPS (production), mostly interactive charting and short summarization calls.
- Bursts: 150–300 QPS for short windows (~2–5 minutes), roughly 4–6 times per hour tied to nightly sync events.
- Avg tokens per request: ~600–700 (prompt + model responses). Some long reports up to 2.5k tokens occasionally (1–2% of requests).
- Streaming: yes — frontend expects partial paragraphs as they become available; UX asks for small chunk latency (<200ms) for first bytes.

2) SLO targets you mentioned
- 95th latency target (generate end-to-end): <= 800ms for interactive flows, 95th.
- Burst latency tolerance: allow degradation to 2s p95 if capacity constrained, provided no errors.

3) What we need from you to finalize sizing
- Confirm the hourly cadence on bursts (how many of those 2–5 minute bursts per hour).
- Attach one week of QPS snapshot if possible (CSV or CT logs) with timestamps and request sizes.
- Indicate whether the long-report requests need streaming output (they can be non-streaming if simpler).

I've attached a small template (requested_workload_template.csv) you can drop data into — if you can send one full day sample or the weekly snapshot that would be ideal. Once we have the CSV Aditya will run a quick model of expected token/sec and concurrency and propose a Dedicated or Hosted configuration and fallback policies.

Proposed next step: 30–45m tech workshop (Aditya + Marissa + 1x infra) next week to walk the sample and confirm the canary plan. What times work for you?

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Greenline throughput mix & burst profile

Thanks, Jasmine — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers / attached sample: 

- Bursts: we see roughly 5 bursts/hour during business hours (09:00–18:00 local), each lasting 2–4 minutes. Nightly syncs add another 2 bursts between 02:00–04:00.
- Steady-state: median 12 QPS (rolling 5m), p95 outside bursts ~20 QPS.
- Peak: observed instantaneous spikes up to ~320 QPS but sustained peak windows are generally 150–260 QPS.
- Tokens: median 610 tokens; 95th ~1,800 tokens due to report generation.
- Streaming: required for our live triaging UI (short answers + progressive hints). For long reports streaming is optional. The UI's desired first-chunk latency is ~150–200ms.

Attached is one week's QPS snapshot (greenline_qps_snapshot.csv) and a short export from our telemetry with per-request token sizes. Please treat the telemetry as internal.

Workshop: Monday or Tuesday next week in the morning (EST) would work — propose Mon 09:30 EST.

Thanks,
Sam White
Director, Product 
Greenline Health
sam.white@greenlinehealth.com

Aditya / Marissa — forwarding Sam's confirmation and the CSV. Key points for sizing and infra follow-up: 

- Workload shape: steady ~12 QPS, bursts 150–260 QPS for 2–4m windows ~5x/hour, occasional spikes to 320 QPS. Avg tokens ~610, p95 ~1800, long reports ~2.5k tokens (rare).
- Streaming required for interactive UI with first-chunk latency target ~150–200ms; long-report streaming optional.
- SLO: p95 generation <=800ms preferred; degrade to 2s in burst tolerated without errors.

Immediate asks for Aditya:
- Run quick throughput estimate assuming: 1) we serve a 7B class model quantized (int8) and 2) a 13B medium quantized profile. Provide expected steady vs burst token/sec and concurrency estimates and recommended node counts (prefer both Hosted and Dedicated options).
- Call out memory/KV cache pressure for 2.5k token outliers and whether we should suggest a short request-routing rule (non-streaming larger reports to a separate non-streaming pool).

For Marissa:
- Prepare a small canary plan and rollback thresholds for the workshop. Suggest traffic shift increments (10/25/50) and monitoring signals (token-level latency, error rate, queue depth).

Let's aim to confirm workshop time with Sam for Mon 09:30 EST (he said mornings work). If Aditya can have the initial numbers by EOD Monday PST, we can walk them in the workshop and propose a Dedicated pool sizing + fallback.

Thanks — Jasmine
